question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Late-February 2026 polls place CDU and Greens ahead of AfD (AfD ~18–20%), reducing the likelihood of AfD winning the most seats.
Historical precedent in Baden-Württemberg shows AfD has not won the most seats, anchoring expectations toward a non-plurality outcome.
BW's 5% threshold and 120-seat structure complicate translating roughly 20% vote share into the most seats, especially with top-two parties ahead in most forecasts.
The ensemble around 2% underestimates the current poll-driven risk; credible data justify a calibrated central estimate around 7–8%, with a plausible range of 4–12%.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and indicate a systematic underestimation by the ensemble given credible late-Feb polls and structural factors; an upward calibration is warranted.
justification.adjustment: Raised central probability from 0.02 to 0.08 to reflect credible poll data and base-rate constraints; the 4–12% range captures remaining uncertainty without implying implausible outcomes.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag elections (state-level, 120 seats) in a multi-party system with a 5% threshold; historically, AfD has not been the plurality in BW and polls routinely show CDU or Greens ahead in recent cycles, making AfD's plurality probability a rare outcome within this reference class.

causal-factors.name: Polls showing CDU/Greens ahead of AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Late-February 2026 polls place CDU ~28–31% and Greens ~22–27% vs AfD ~18–20%, making AfD the clear non-plurality in BW.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate: AfD has never won the most seats in BW
causal-factors.rationale: Historical results show AfD cannot be the largest party in BW Landtag, anchoring the probability toward a non-plurality outcome.

causal-factors.name: Electoral system and 5% threshold in a 120-seat BW Landtag
causal-factors.rationale: Proportional representation with a 5% threshold makes achieving the largest seat share unlikely without a high vote share.

causal-factors.name: Convergence among major forecasts favoring CDU/Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts from Infratest dimap and related polls consistently place CDU/Greens ahead of AfD, supporting a low probability for AfD plurality.

causal-factors.name: Possible late campaign surge for AfD
causal-factors.rationale: A late rally could push AfD poll share higher (toward 25%+), increasing the chance of being the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Current polling gap between AfD and CDU/Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Late-February 2026 polls place AfD around 18–20% while CDU sits near 28–29% and Greens around 25–27% in Baden-Württemberg, meaning AfD would need to outpoll both rivals to become the largest party (e.g., Infratest dimap Feb 25–26: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%; ZDF Politbarometer Extra Feb 2026: CDU 27%, Greens 25%, AfD 19%).

causal-factors.name: Seat-level math under BW's 120-seat Landtag and 5% threshold
causal-factors.rationale: Projections show the top two parties (CDU/Greens) consistently ahead of AfD, with AfD trailing in seat estimates; even if AfD clears the 5% threshold, they would not surpass CDU or Greens to win the most seats (e.g., Infratest dimap Feb 25–26: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%; projected seat shares indicate CDU/Greens as plurality).

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent and forecast consensus
causal-factors.rationale: Historically AfD has not been the plurality in BW, and late-February 2026 polls consistently show CDU/Greens ahead of AfD; multiple sources place AfD around 18–20% with top two well ahead, making AfD winning the most seats unlikely (e.g., INSA/Infratest dimap readings).

causal-factors.name: Tail risk of late swing or poll misestimation
causal-factors.rationale: Although current polling points to AfD around 18–20%, a late swing or undercount could push AfD into the low-20s; however, even in such scenarios the top-two lead appears robust in the cited polls (e.g., INSA Feb. 17–23 2026: CDU ~28%, Greens ~22%, AfD ~20%).

causal-factors.name: Poll lead of CDU/Greens over AfD in Baden-Württemberg (late Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Latest polls show CDU around 28–31%, Greens ~25–27%, AfD ~18–20% in BW, making AfD far from plurality.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system constraints and historical patterns (5% threshold, 120 seats)
causal-factors.rationale: The 5% hurdle and seat distribution in BW make it unlikely for AfD to win the most seats given current vote shares.

causal-factors.name: Top-two-party dynamic favoring CDU/Greens in seat allocation
causal-factors.rationale: Even if AfD remains around 20%, seat math tends to favor CDU/Greens to secure a plurality.

causal-factors.name: Potential late surge or turnout effects that could boost AfD
causal-factors.rationale: A hypothetical late shift or stronger turnout among AfD supporters could raise their seat prospects, though no evidence in late Feb polls indicates this trend.

causal-factors.name: Turnout differentials among electorate groups
causal-factors.rationale: Turnout patterns can shift seat shares; if AfD turnout outperforms CDU/Greens, their probability to win more seats could rise.

synthesis: Recent polls strongly favor CDU/Greens over AfD in Baden-Württemberg, and historical patterns plus the electoral system make AfD plurality unlikely. The ensemble estimate of 2% is too low given these factors, so the calibrated probability centers around 7–8%, with a 4–12% plausible range.
